newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS--API's likely to show another heat oil build.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS--API's likely to show another heat oil build.

text.p: This week's inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) is likely to show heating oil stocks rose last week, but once again, the extent of any build will be key to the market's flavor, traders said.
"A build of less than one million barrels will be disappointing to anyone who is short this market," said Thomas Blakeslee, analyst at Cargill Investor Services in New York.
Crude oil and gasoline stocks were meanwhile seen falling, and a combination of refinery glitches and turnarounds were seen bringing refinery utilzation rates down as well.

Blakeslee's prediction of a distillate build of anywhere from 500,000 to 1.5 million barrels was about the average, with only one trader suggesting distillate stocks could fall. Distillate stocks stood at 113.6 million in the last survey.
Traders generally saw lightening volumes of distillate exports to Europe as the main reason for their forecasts for higher distillate stocks.
"The export statistics are going to be the big variable," said Victor Yu, vice president of futures trading at Refco.
If lower exports will fuel a distillate stock build, lower crude imports will help crude stocks fall, traders said.
"Crude stocks are anticipated to decline due primarily to the recent closure of the arbitrage window with Europe," said Jim Ritterbusch, a trader with Sweeney Oil Co in Chicago.
Crude stocks were seen falling by one million barrels from the 302.3 million barrels recorded in the previous report.

One caveat traders attached to their crude predictions was the drop in refinery utilization rates they also forecasted, which could mean crude stocks piled up a bit, and some sources predicted a rise in crude stocks for this very reason.
Refinery run rates were called one percentage point lower from the 94.9 percent level recorded in the last API report.
Traders meanwhile said the drop in refinery runs, related to refinery production difficulties and autumn maintenance programs, was meanwhile seen boosting gasoline's bullish fortunes, traders said.
Gasoline stocks were seen falling one million barrels from the prior-week levels of 196.3 million, helped also by views that imports are likely to continue to be light, traders said.

"Gasoline demand was understated last (time). This report will show steady demand with low output. I also think you will see lower imports," said Tom Bentz, analyst with ING Derivatives Clearing in New York.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
